requires.title: reach the database
requires.consequence: nothing can connect at all

requires.title: read every table, view and sequence
privileges: SELECT on each table and sequence
requires.consequence: pg_dump stops on the first table it cannot lock, and the dump is not written

requires.title: see every row of a table with row-level security
requires.consequence: pg_dump sets row_security to off so that it dumps whole tables, and a role that cannot bypass the policy fails rather than silently dumping a subset

applies.subject: a table that has row-level security enabled

requires.title: read the large objects
requires.consequence: pg_dump carries large objects by default and stops on the first one it cannot open
requires.grant: -- per object: GRANT SELECT ON LARGE OBJECT <oid> TO {role};

requires.title: create a schema
requires.consequence: a restore stops at the first CREATE SCHEMA in the dump

requires.title: enter and create in every schema
requires.consequence: a restore stops partway with `permission denied for schema` — on PostgreSQL 15 and newer this bites on `public`, which no longer grants CREATE to everybody
requires.grant: GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO {role};

requires.title: own the database
requires.consequence: `sloop db drop` is refused with `must be owner of database`, after everything else about the run has already worked

requires.title: create the extensions this database uses
requires.consequence: a dump of this database carries CREATE EXTENSION for an extension PostgreSQL does not mark trusted, and only a superuser can run that — restoring elsewhere needs the extension installed first

applies.subject: an extension that is not trusted

requires.grant: -- a superuser runs: CREATE EXTENSION <name>; on the destination first

requires.title: read every table
requires.consequence: the dump program cannot read the rows, and fails before writing anything

requires.title: read the view definitions
requires.consequence: the dump program stops on the first view with `SHOW VIEW command denied`

requires.title: read the trigger definitions
requires.consequence: the dump program exits 0 and the dump carries no triggers. Nothing in the output says so

requires.title: read the event definitions
requires.consequence: the dump program stops on `show events` with `Access denied`

requires.title: read a stored routine it did not define
requires.consequence: the dump program exits 0 and writes a dump with every stored routine missing from it. Nothing in the output says so: a backup that looks fine has quietly lost every function and procedure

applies.subject: a stored routine defined by another account

requires.title: create the tables and load the rows
requires.consequence: the restore stops partway, leaving the destination half built
requires.grant: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, CREATE, DROP, ALTER, REFERENCES, LOCK TABLES ON {database}.* TO {role};

requires.title: create the views
requires.consequence: the restore stops at the first view

requires.title: create the triggers
requires.consequence: the restore stops at the first trigger

requires.title: create the stored routines
requires.consequence: the restore stops at the first routine
requires.grant: GRANT CREATE ROUTINE, ALTER ROUTINE ON {database}.* TO {role};

requires.title: create the events
requires.consequence: the restore stops at the first event

requires.title: create a stored function while binary logging is on
requires.consequence: the restore stops with `You do not have the SUPER privilege and binary logging is enabled`. The alternative is for a DBA to set log_bin_trust_function_creators on the destination server

applies.subject: a stored function, while the server has binary logging on and log_bin_trust_function_creators off

requires.title: delete the database itself
requires.consequence: `sloop db drop` is refused with `Access denied`, after everything else about the run has already worked

waives.because: sloop dumps with --single-transaction, which takes no locks on the source
sloop dumps with --no-tablespaces, so nothing reads INFORMATION_SCHEMA.FILES
sloop dumps with --set-gtid-purged=OFF, so a GTID-enabled server needs neither
